title: Scrambled Eggs with Smoked Salmon
description: Silky, creamy scrambled eggs paired with smoked salmon and fresh chives. High in protein, ready in under 10 minutes — the ultimate high-performance breakfast.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Crack eggs into a bowl, add milk, salt and pepper. Whisk until combined.
2. Heat butter in a non-stick pan over low-medium heat.
3. Pour in egg mixture. Using a silicone spatula, gently push eggs from the edges toward the centre in slow folds.
4. Remove from heat while eggs still look slightly underdone — residual heat finishes them.
5. Plate and top with smoked salmon and fresh chives.
equipment:
Non-stick pan
Silicone spatula
Bowl
Whisk
notes: The key to creamy scrambled eggs is low heat and patience. Never stop stirring or you'll get rubbery curds.

title: Greek Yogurt Parfait with Oats & Berries
description: Creamy Greek yogurt layered with rolled oats, fresh mixed berries, and a drizzle of honey. Protein-rich, no cooking required, and ready in 5 minutes.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Spoon Greek yogurt into a glass or bowl.
2. Top with rolled oats, mixed berries, and honey.
3. Serve immediately, or refrigerate overnight for a softer oat texture.
notes: Use full-fat Greek yogurt for the best texture and satiety. Berries can be fresh or frozen (thawed).

title: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
description: Crushed avocado on toasted wholegrain bread, topped with a perfectly poached egg and chilli flakes. A modern classic that delivers healthy fats and protein in one slice.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
2. Bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar. Crack egg into a small cup, then lower into the simmering water. Cook 3 minutes for a runny yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon.
3. Halve the avocado, remove stone, and scoop flesh into a bowl. Add lemon juice, salt and pepper. Crush with a fork, leaving some texture.
4. Spread crushed avocado on toast. Top with poached egg, chilli flakes, and extra salt.
equipment:
Small saucepan
Slotted spoon
Toaster
Fork
notes: A splash of white vinegar in the poaching water helps the egg white hold together. Fresh eggs poach best.

title: Overnight Oats
description: Thick, creamy oats soaked overnight in milk with chia seeds and topped with banana slices. Zero morning effort — prep the night before and grab from the fridge.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. In a jar or container, combine oats, milk, chia seeds, and honey. Stir well.
2. Seal and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
3. In the morning, top with sliced banana and serve cold.
notes: Add a tablespoon of peanut butter for extra protein and flavour. Keeps for up to 3 days in the fridge.

title: Banana Protein Pancakes
description: Fluffy three-ingredient pancakes made from banana, eggs, and oats — no flour, no sugar. High protein, naturally sweet, and genuinely delicious.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. In a bowl, mash banana until smooth.
2. Add eggs and rolled oats. Mix until a thick batter forms.
3. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a little coconut oil.
4. Pour about 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook 1 minute.
5. Serve with a drizzle of honey or fresh berries.
notes: Let the batter rest 2 minutes before cooking so the oats absorb moisture. Add a scoop of protein powder for extra protein.

title: Egg & Vegetable Omelette
description: A classic three-egg omelette filled with sautéed mushrooms, spinach, and cherry tomatoes. Wholesome, fast, and endlessly adaptable.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Whisk eggs with salt and pepper in a bowl.
2. Heat butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms, cook 3 minutes until golden. Add spinach and cherry tomatoes, cook 1 minute. Transfer filling to a plate.
3. Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining butter. Pour in egg mixture. Tilt the pan so eggs coat the surface.
4. When edges set and top is still slightly glossy, add the filling to one half.
5. Fold omelette in half and slide onto plate. Serve immediately.
notes: Don't overcook — the inside should stay just set. Use any vegetables you have on hand.

title: Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick, creamy blended bowl of frozen banana and mixed berries, topped with granola, sliced banana, and chia seeds. Vibrant, nutritious, and incredibly filling.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Blend frozen banana and mixed berries with oat milk until thick and smooth. Add a splash more oat milk if needed — the consistency should be thicker than a drinkable smoothie.
2. Pour into a bowl.
3. Top with granola, sliced banana, and chia seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Use frozen fruit for a thick, creamy consistency. Do not add too much liquid or it becomes a drinkable smoothie.

title: Cottage Cheese Toast with Berries
description: Thick-sliced sourdough topped with creamy cottage cheese and fresh berries. Simple, high-protein, and satisfying without any cooking.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Toast the sourdough bread.
2. Spread cottage cheese generously on each slice.
3. Top with fresh berries and a drizzle of honey.
notes: Full-fat cottage cheese has the best texture. Strawberries, blueberries, or raspberries all work equally well.

title: Turkey & Veggie Breakfast Wrap
description: A warm flour tortilla filled with scrambled eggs, turkey slices, avocado, and salsa. Portable, high-protein, and genuinely filling — ideal for busy mornings.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Whisk eggs with salt and pepper. Scramble in a non-stick pan over low-medium heat.
2. Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
3. Lay turkey slices on the tortilla, add scrambled eggs, avocado slices, and salsa.
4. Fold sides in and roll tightly. Serve immediately.
notes: Make it ahead — wrap in foil and reheat in the oven at 180°C for 8 minutes.

title: Ricotta Toast with Honey & Walnuts
description: Creamy ricotta on toasted wholegrain bread, drizzled with honey and scattered with walnuts. An elegant, satisfying breakfast with healthy fats and protein.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Toast the bread until golden.
2. Spread ricotta generously on each slice.
3. Drizzle with honey and scatter crushed walnuts on top.
notes: Use a good-quality ricotta for best flavour. The walnut-honey combination is classic and excellent.

title: Classic Chicken Curry
description: A fragrant, rich chicken curry with tender pieces of chicken simmered in a golden coconut-tomato sauce. Warmly spiced with cumin, coriander, and turmeric — perfect for a cozy weeknight dinner.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Prepare the aromatics
1. Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
2. Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
GroupName : Build the sauce
3. Stir in curry powder, cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Toast spices for 30 seconds.
4. Add diced tomatoes and coconut milk. Stir to combine.
5. Season with salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
GroupName : Cook the chicken
6. Add cubed chicken breast. Stir to coat in the sauce.
7. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve over basmati rice.
equipment:
Large skillet or Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
For a richer curry, use chicken thighs instead of breast.
Add a handful of spinach at the end for extra nutrition.
Leftovers taste even better the next day as the flavours deepen.

title: Classic Bolognese
description: A slow-cooked Italian meat sauce that clings beautifully to tagliatelle or pappardelle. Made with a soffritto base, ground beef, and a splash of milk for silky richness.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Soffritto base
1. Heat olive oil and butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
2. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly golden.
GroupName : Brown the meat
3. Add ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until no pink remains, about 8 minutes.
GroupName : Build the sauce
4. Pour in white wine and cook until evaporated, about 3 minutes.
5. Add whole milk, stir, and cook until absorbed, about 5 minutes.
6. Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
7. Add canned crushed tomatoes. Stir to combine. Reduce heat to very low.
8. Simmer uncovered for 1.5–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thick and rich.
9. Taste, adjust seasoning. Serve over fresh tagliatelle with grated Parmigiano.
equipment:
Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
The longer the simmer, the better the bolognese. Don't rush it.
Freeze the sauce in portions for up to 3 months.

title: Hearty Beef Stew
description: A soul-warming beef stew with melt-in-your-mouth chunks of braised beef, tender vegetables, and a deep, glossy wine-enriched broth.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Prep and sear
1. Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
2. Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides, 3–4 minutes per batch. Set aside.
3. Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
4. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 1 minute.
GroupName : Build the stew
5. Pour in red wine, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.
6. Add beef broth, thyme, bay leaves, and Worcestershire sauce. Return beef to pot.
7. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours.
GroupName : Add vegetables
8. Add potatoes and carrots. Cook uncovered for 30 more minutes until vegetables are tender.
9. Mix cornstarch with 45 ml cold water, stir into stew to thicken.
10. Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Serve in bowls.
equipment:
Large Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
Use a well-marbled cut like chuck roast for the best texture.
Make it a day ahead; it tastes even better reheated.

title: Baked Salmon with Roasted Vegetables
description: Oven-baked salmon fillets with a honey-mustard glaze alongside roasted broccoli and sweet potato. Clean, protein-packed, and on the table in 30 minutes.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Mix honey, Dijon mustard, olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper to make the glaze.
3. Toss sweet potato and broccoli with olive oil and salt. Spread on one half of the baking sheet.
4. Place salmon fillets on the other half. Brush with the honey-mustard glaze.
5. Roast for 20–25 minutes until salmon is cooked through and vegetables are golden.
6. Serve immediately.
equipment:
Baking sheet
Parchment paper
Small bowl
notes: Salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork and the thickest part has turned opaque. Do not overcook.

title: Grilled Chicken & Quinoa Bowl
description: Marinated, grilled chicken breast over fluffy quinoa with baby spinach, roasted cherry tomatoes, and a lemon-tahini dressing. Clean, balanced, and meal-prep-friendly.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Mix olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for the marinade. Coat chicken breasts and marinate at least 15 minutes.
2. Cook quinoa: bring 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa to a boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
3. Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Grill chicken 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
4. For the dressing, mix tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and water until smooth.
5. Divide quinoa among bowls. Top with spinach, sliced chicken, cherry tomatoes. Drizzle with dressing.
equipment:
Grill pan or skillet
Small saucepan
Bowls
notes: Cook extra quinoa and store for the week. The bowls keep for 3 days in the fridge if dressing is stored separately.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached directly in a spiced, fragrant tomato and pepper sauce. A Middle Eastern classic that comes together in one pan and is perfect any time of day.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a wide skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
2. Add onion and pepper. Cook 8 minutes until soft.
3. Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and chilli flakes. Cook 1 minute.
4. Add crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Season with salt. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
5. Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
6. Cover and cook 5–8 minutes until whites are set but yolks are still runny.
7. Scatter with crumbled feta and fresh parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
equipment:
Wide skillet or cast-iron pan
Lid
notes: Don't rush the sauce — let it simmer until deep red and thick before adding eggs. Serve directly from the pan at the table.

title: Turkey Meatballs with Marinara
description: Juicy oven-baked turkey meatballs simmered in a classic tomato marinara, served over whole wheat spaghetti. High-protein, lower in fat than beef meatballs, and great for meal prep.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Make the meatballs
1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a bowl, combine ground turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Mix well.
3. Roll into 20 g balls and arrange on the baking sheet.
4. Bake 18–20 minutes until golden and cooked through.
GroupName : Marinara & assembly
5. Heat olive oil in a saucepan. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add crushed tomatoes, salt, basil, and sugar. Simmer 15 minutes.
6. Add baked meatballs to the marinara. Simmer together 5 minutes.
7. Cook pasta according to package directions. Serve meatballs and sauce over pasta.
equipment:
Baking sheet
Parchment paper
Large saucepan
Large pot for pasta
notes: Meatballs and sauce freeze perfectly for up to 3 months. Cook pasta fresh when serving.

title: Lentil & Vegetable Soup
description: A hearty, warming red lentil soup packed with tomatoes, carrots, and cumin. Thick, filling, and completely plant-based — exceptional value for a vegan high-protein meal.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and carrot. Cook 8 minutes until soft.
2. Add garlic, cumin, coriander, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute.
3. Add red lentils, crushed tomatoes, and vegetable broth. Season with salt.
4. Bring to a boil, then simmer 25–30 minutes until lentils are completely soft and soup is thick.
5. Add lemon juice. Use a stick blender to partially blend for a creamier texture, or leave chunky.
6. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with crusty bread.
notes: Red lentils cook quickly and do not need soaking. The soup thickens as it sits — add extra broth when reheating.

title: Chicken & Brown Rice Stir-Fry
description: Tender chicken strips wok-fried with broccoli, carrots, and snap peas in a savoury soy-ginger sauce, served over brown rice. Fast, clean, and high-protein.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Cook brown rice according to package directions.
2. Whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, honey, and cornstarch for the sauce.
3. Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add chicken strips. Stir-fry 4–5 minutes until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
4. Add broccoli and carrots to the wok. Stir-fry 3 minutes. Add snap peas, cook 1 minute more.
5. Return chicken to the wok. Pour over the sauce. Toss everything together and cook 1–2 minutes until sauce thickens.
6. Serve over brown rice. Garnish with sesame seeds.
equipment:
Wok or large skillet
Saucepan for rice
Whisk
notes: High heat is essential for a good stir-fry — don't crowd the pan or the chicken will steam instead of sear.

title: Black Bean Tacos
description: Crispy corn tortillas filled with seasoned black beans, red cabbage slaw, avocado, and a lime-cilantro crema. Vibrant, filling, and entirely plant-based.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Drain and rinse black beans. In a pan over medium heat with olive oil, add beans, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt and a splash of water. Cook 5 minutes, mashing slightly.
2. Mix red cabbage, lime juice, and a pinch of salt for the slaw.
3. Mash avocado with lime juice, garlic powder, and salt.
4. Warm tortillas in a dry pan.
5. Assemble tacos: layer beans, cabbage slaw, avocado mash, and garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Add sliced pickled jalapeños for heat. The beans can be made ahead and reheated.

title: Pesto Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
description: Tender chicken breasts coated in basil pesto, baked alongside crispy roasted potatoes and cherry tomatoes. Simple, flavour-forward, and effortlessly elegant.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Toss potatoes with olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread on the baking sheet. Roast 15 minutes.
3. Coat chicken breasts with pesto. Nestle among the potatoes along with cherry tomatoes.
4. Return to oven and roast a further 20–25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are golden and crisp.
5. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use shop-bought pesto to keep this recipe fast. Homemade pesto takes it to another level if you have the time.

title: Tuna Nicoise Salad
description: A substantial French salad with canned tuna, hard-boiled eggs, green beans, olives, and potatoes in a Dijon vinaigrette. Protein-rich, no hot cooking required, and ready in 20 minutes.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Boil potatoes 12 minutes until tender. In the last 3 minutes add green beans. Drain and run under cold water.
2. Boil eggs 8 minutes, transfer to ice water, peel and halve.
3. For the dressing: whisk Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper.
4. Arrange lettuce on a platter. Top with potatoes, green beans, tuna (drained, broken into chunks), hard-boiled egg halves, olives, and cherry tomatoes.
5. Drizzle dressing over the top and serve.
notes: Tuna in olive oil gives the best flavour. Don't overdress — the salad should taste bright, not oily.

title: Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry
description: A thick, warming curry with tender chickpeas and sweet potato cubes in a spiced coconut sauce. Completely vegan, excellent for meal prep, and better the next day.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook 8 minutes until golden.
2. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and chilli flakes. Cook 1 minute.
3. Add sweet potato and chickpeas. Stir to coat in spices.
4. Pour in coconut milk and diced tomatoes. Season with salt.
5. Simmer 20–25 minutes until sweet potato is tender.
6. Squeeze in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
7. Serve with basmati rice or naan, topped with fresh cilantro.
equipment:
Large pot or Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
notes: Add a handful of baby spinach in the last 2 minutes for extra greens. This curry freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Apple with Almond Butter
description: Crisp apple slices alongside a generous portion of natural almond butter. A perfectly balanced snack with natural sugars and healthy fats to keep energy levels stable.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Slice the apple into wedges.
2. Serve with almond butter for dipping.
notes: Use natural almond butter with no added sugar or oil. Peanut butter works equally well.

title: Hummus with Vegetable Crudités
description: Creamy hummus served with an assortment of raw vegetables — carrots, celery, and bell pepper — for dipping. A classic high-fibre, plant-based snack.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Cut carrots, celery, and bell pepper into sticks.
2. Serve with hummus for dipping.
notes: Use good-quality hummus. Make your own from chickpeas, tahini, lemon, and garlic for even better results.

title: Hard-Boiled Eggs with Cherry Tomatoes
description: A simple, protein-packed snack of hard-boiled eggs alongside sweet cherry tomatoes. One of the most effective snacks for keeping hunger at bay.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water by 3 cm. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 8–10 minutes.
2. Transfer immediately to ice water for 5 minutes. Peel and halve.
3. Serve with cherry tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
notes: Boil a batch at the start of the week and keep them unpeeled in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Homemade Granola Bars
description: Chewy, dense granola bars made with oats, honey, almond butter, and dark chocolate chips. No baking needed — press together and refrigerate. Great for on-the-go.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine oats, almond butter, honey, and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined.
2. Fold in dark chocolate chips and crushed almonds.
3. Line a 20×20 cm baking tin with parchment paper. Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the tin.
4. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
5. Slice into 8 bars. Store wrapped in the fridge for up to 1 week.
equipment:
Large bowl
20×20 cm baking tin
Parchment paper
notes: Press the mixture very firmly into the tin — this is what makes the bars hold together without baking.

title: Mixed Nuts & Dried Fruit
description: A handful of mixed nuts with a small portion of dried apricots. The simplest, most reliable snack for steady energy between meals.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Weigh out nuts and dried apricots. Combine in a small bowl or bag.
2. Eat as is.
notes: Portion control matters — weigh your nuts rather than guessing, as they are very calorie-dense.

title: Protein Smoothie
description: A thick, creamy smoothie with banana, Greek yogurt, and oat milk. Naturally sweet, genuinely filling, and can be prepared in under 3 minutes.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a blender.
2. Blend on high for 45 seconds until completely smooth.
3. Serve immediately.
notes: Use a frozen banana for a thicker, colder smoothie. Add a tablespoon of almond butter for extra protein and healthy fats.

title: Rice Cakes with Avocado
description: Light rice cakes spread with mashed avocado, lemon juice, and a pinch of chilli flakes. Low-calorie crunch with healthy fats — ideal as a light snack slot.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Mash avocado with lemon juice and a pinch of salt until smooth.
2. Spread on rice cakes. Dust with chilli flakes.
notes: Use ripe avocado. Eat immediately after assembling to prevent browning.
